facts.label: Achar o banheiro
facts.sub: Peça com “Excuse me” e ouça a resposta: esquerda ou direita, no fundo, perto da escada. Alguns lugares dão chave ou senha só para clientes.

facts.label: A palavra certa
facts.sub: Nos EUA, a palavra mais comum e educada em lugares públicos é restroom ou bathroom. Toilet existe, mas costuma falar do vaso sanitário. Pergunte assim: “Excuse me, where’s the restroom?” e agradeça a resposta.

facts.label: Só para clientes
facts.sub: Em muitas lojas pequenas e cafés, o banheiro é para clientes. Às vezes há uma chave com etiqueta grande ou uma senha no recibo. Se você comprou algo, diga isso com calma e peça: “Can I have the key?”

compare.br: In Brazil, you ask for the banheiro, and some cafés and shops also keep it for customers.
compare.us: In the USA, you can say restroom or bathroom. Many places are free, but some small shops want you to buy something first.
compare.ask: How do you ask for the restroom in English?

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In the USA, people often say “restroom” or “bathroom”.
items.why: These words are common and polite.

items.s: Every shop has a restroom open to everyone.
items.why: Some places keep it for customers only.

items.s: Some places give you a key or a code for the restroom.
items.why: This helps keep the room for customers.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

pages.title: The key to the restroom · 1/3
paragraphs: Dan is in a small coffee shop in Chicago. He has a cup of coffee in his hand. Now he needs the restroom, but he does not see a sign.

He goes to the counter. “**Excuse me, where's the restroom?**” he asks. “**It's at the back of the store**,” the worker says. “**Is it on the left or the right?**” “**On the right, next to the stairs.**”

pages.title: The key to the restroom · 2/3
paragraphs: “**Is it free?**” Dan asks. “**It's for customers only.**” “**I bought a coffee**,” Dan says, and he shows his cup. The worker smiles. “**Then you can use it. Here's the key.**”
The key is big and heavy, with a wooden tag. “**Is there a code?**” Dan asks. “No, the door has a lock. Just use the key,” the worker says. Dan says thanks and walks to the back.

paragraphs: Dan finds the door near the stairs. He thinks of a TV show for children, “Mr. Benn.” In it, a man goes into a costume shop and opens a special door. Dan laughs. His door is not magic, but it is a very good door today. He puts the key back on the counter.

pages.focus: os sons de L e R: left x right
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em inglês, left e right são diferentes só pelo L e pelo R. Brasileiros costumam trocar o R inglês pelo som de “rr” ou de “h”, e isso pode confundir quando você pergunta direções.
pages.how: Para o L, toque a ponta da língua atrás dos dentes de cima. Para o R, puxe a língua para trás e arredonde os lábios, sem encostar em nada, como em “rrright”.
pages.tip: Treine devagar: light, right, light, right. Depois diga a frase inteira.
